data.title: Rupee declines 23 paise to 92.85 against US dollar during early trade
data.description:
The rupee saw heightened volatility and tumbled 23 paise to 92.85 against the US dollar in early trade on Monday, tracking a selling trend in domestic equity markets.

Easing crude oil prices helped the local currency initially, but it soon came under pressure due to a firm American currency, forex traders said.

At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 93.47 and climbed up to 92.43 before trading at 92.85 against the greenback, down 23 paise from its previous close.

On Friday, the rupee sustained its ascending order for the fifth consecutive session to settle 70 paise higher at 92.62 against the US dollar. The unit reclaimed above the 93 level for the first time since April 10.

 

The local unit has logged a sharp appreciation of over 1.6 per cent in the past five back-to-back sessions since the closing level of 94.19 against the greenback recorded on November 13.

Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was at 103.71, lower by 0.03 per cent.

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.28 per cent lower at $92.38 per barrel in futures trade.

On the domestic equity market front, Sensex declined 408.30 points or 0.49 per cent to 83,511.41 in early trade, while Nifty fell 118.90 points or 0.46 per cent to 25,684.30.

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought equities worth ₹10,308.42 crore on a net basis on Friday, according to exchange data.

The latest data released by the Reserve Bank of India on Friday showed the country's forex reserves dropped $14.205 billion to $705.342 billion in the week ended November 13. In the previous reporting week, the overall reserves had jumped $2.49 billion to $719.547 billion.

According to the Commerce and Industry Ministry data released on Friday, output of key infrastructure industries rose 10.9 per cent in October, the fastest pace in the new series, driven by double-digit growth in coal, iron ore, electricity and cement production. Production expanded by 0.8 per cent in October last year and 8.2 per cent in September 2026.

data.title: Rupee could rise to 91.50/$ on equity inflows: HDFC Bank's treasury head
data.description:
The Indian rupee could gain to 91.50 against the US dollar if equity inflows remain strong and geopolitical risks stay in check, a top treasury official at the country's ​largest private bank said.

The Indian currency depreciated sharply till October, declining 8% against the ​US dollar at the lowest point of the year as foreign investors withdrew from equity markets in ‌Asia's third-largest economy due to high valuations and lack of AI investments.

Higher oil prices added to the pressure, prompting tough measures from the central bank, including a reserve requirement against large hedging transactions.

Markets turned in November, with global investors pumping a monthly record $12 billion into Indian equities.

 

"I believe 91.50 could be a possibility," said Arup Rakshit, group head for treasury at HDFC Bank in Mumbai in an interview late on Friday, adding that he sees the currency trading in a range of 91.50 to 93.50 in the near term.

On Friday, the rupee closed at 92.67 to the dollar.

The rupee has gained nearly 2.5% in November, turning sentiment in the offshore non-deliverable forwards market and prompting exporters to sell dollars, Rakshit said.

Additional dollar demand brought on by the Reserve Bank of ‌India's decision to impose a 20% foreign exchange risk reserve on large hedging transactions has also eased, he added.

"When the Reserve Bank of India introduced a foreign exchange risk reserve there was some additional dollar demand that came in from importers as absolute hedged import rates were lower, since the INR had immediately appreciated," Rakshit said.

"That demand is now reducing as the import cycle is typically 90 days and nearly half of that is over," he said, adding that importers are hedging less as the rupee strengthens and oil prices fall.

A 50 BASIS POINT HIKE?

While pressure on ​the currency has eased, inflation has breached the central bank's upper tolerance limit of 6%, prompting a few analysts to expect ‌a 50 basis point hike at its December meeting.

Rakshit does not rule this out.

"I think the repo rate will settle somewhere between 6.25-6.5%. A 25 basis point hike in December is more or less given. There ​is a section ‌of the market which is thinking it could be a 50 basis point hike and I would lean on that ‌side," he said.

Retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October and wholesale inflation rose to 12.3%.

Higher wholesale prices have yet to fully pass through into retail prices, Rakshit said, adding that food prices are also starting to rise.

This will ‌prompt ​the central bank ​to raise rates and keep liquidity tight at 0.6% to 1% of banking system deposits, he said.

Bond yields would also rise, but not sharply, he said.

"Immediately, I would put the top for the 10-year ‌at about 7.40% and ​then moving up to 7.50% to 7.60 levels max. I don't see it going beyond that," he said.

data.title: India's ties with Russia can help push for end to Ukraine war: Dutch FM
data.description:
The Netherlands views India's continued engagement with Russia as an "added value," as New Delhi can use its ties with Moscow to persuade it to end the war in Ukraine, Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen has said.

Berendsen is on an official visit to India from November 22 to 23. He co-chaired the inaugural Foreign Ministers' Meeting with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in New Delhi on Sunday and reviewed the India-Netherlands Strategic Partnership.

"We understand that India has its own history, its own role in the world and its own relations," Berendsen told PTI on Sunday, responding to a question on India's strategic autonomy and its continued engagement with Moscow.

 

"We actually see it as an added value of our relationship with India that it has a relationship with Russia and can also use that relationship to show Russia that it needs to put an end to this war and accept a ceasefire," he said.

The Russia-Ukraine war, in its fifth year, continues with intensified attacks from both sides. Russia has stepped up strikes on Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure, while US-brokered peace talks have made little progress beyond a prisoner swap.

Berendsen said India and the Netherlands, as trading countries, shared concerns over maritime security and freedom of navigation, and needed to work together to address challenges in an increasingly uncertain world.

"I think we're dealing with the same challenges: how to decrease dependencies, how to be more strategically autonomous on critical raw materials, technology and energy," he said.

"If you want to do that, you need to diversify, which means new partnerships. I think the Netherlands, the EU and India are doing exactly that," he added.

On trade, he described the proposed India-European Union free trade agreement, expected to be signed in December, as a crucial step that could open opportunities beyond merchandise trade.

Berendsen also welcomed the memorandum of understanding (MoU) between Tata Electronics and Dutch semiconductor major ASML, saying cooperation in the semiconductor ecosystem offered significant possibilities for both countries.

The MoU was signed in May during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to the Netherlands to support India's first commercial 300 mm (12-inch) semiconductor fabrication plant in Dholera, Gujarat.

"...it is not only about signing a document; it is the starting point of strengthening the partnership, so we are taking the next steps," Berendsen told reporters at a press conference after his meeting with Jaishankar.

Berendsen said his meeting with Jaishankar was their sixth this year, reflecting the growing engagement between the two countries. He said cooperation was being strengthened in sectors such as energy, security, technology, water management and agriculture.

Jaishankar and his Dutch counterpart on Sunday discussed the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war and the situation in the Black Sea, with Berendsen appreciating India's efforts towards facilitating a possible arrangement for safe passage of grain shipments through the region.

The remarks come amid increasing attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea during the Russia-Ukraine war.

Berendsen said the war had affected global food security and the Netherlands valued India's role in working towards a solution.

In his opening remarks at the meeting, Jaishankar said the two sides had elevated their relationship to a Strategic Partnership and were looking to expand cooperation in areas including semiconductors, technology, defence and renewable energy, while continuing their traditional collaboration in water, agriculture and health.

"There are shared challenges. I think terrorism is one, climate change is another, where it's important we work together. So I'm really pleased today to have this chance to co-chair our inaugural dialogue mechanism for reviewing the strategic partnership," Jaishankar said.

Berendsen is scheduled to meet Electronics and Information Technology Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Monday before departing from India.

data.title: ICICI Prudential AMC seeks $800 million as alternatives push grows
data.description:
By Saikat Das and Baiju Kalesh
 
ICICI Prudential Asset Management Co. is seeking as much as $800 million for private credit and special opportunities funds, according to people familiar with the matter, tapping growing demand for alternative assets from wealthy investors and institutions.
 
The Indian money manager aims to close its third private credit fund at about $500 million in December and is separately seeking up to $300 million for a special opportunities vehicle, said the people, who asked not to be identified because the information is private.
 
The potential fundraising underscores the growth of private credit in Asia, which has largely avoided turmoil elsewhere as funds tend to be closed-ended and have limited software exposure. Indian managers have raised billions of dollars and are taking a growing share of the country’s lending deals from global firms, intensifying competition for managers such as Bain Capital and Davidson Kempner Capital Management.
 
 
ICICI Prudential Corporate Credit Opportunities Fund has received commitments from more than a dozen insurance companies as well as family offices and wealthy individuals, said the people. The fund focuses on performing credit rather than distressed situations, typically providing capital to borrowers for expansion and other capital expenditure, they said.
 
A spokesperson at ICICI Prudential AMC declined to comment. The firm is backed by ICICI Bank Ltd. and Prudential Plc. The UK-listed insurer owns about a third of the Indian money manager through Prudential Corp.
 
ICICI Prudential AMC’s latest vehicle follows two private credit funds that raised about $160 million and $330 million, respectively, the people said. The manager has deployed money in companies including GMR Group, Puravankara Ltd. and Pinnacle Industries Ltd., the people said. The companies did not respond to emails seeking comment.

data.title: India, Iran hold bilateral talks on cultural cooperation during SCO forum
data.description:
India and Iran held bilateral talks on the sidelines of the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum to bolster cultural cooperation, Union Culture Secretary Vivek Aggarwal said on Sunday.

At a press interaction held at the venue, the historic Purana Quila, shortly before the closure of the session, asked if any formal bilateral talks were held between India and Pakistan on the sidelines, Aggarwal said, "There were no formal bilateral talks between the two sides." However, he said that members of the Indian side did have interactions with him over banquets and during the conference, as well as there were other "informal discussions" with him during the course of the forum, as with other ministers too.

 

"In general, there were also meetings between ministers and heads of delegations, as the aim of this (multilateral) forum is to exchange views, so there were many meetings, and a lot of things were discussed," the culture secretary said.

However, he didn't specify how many bilateral talks took place during the course of the Forum hosted by India from November 20-22.

Asked if any bilateral meeting took place with Iran, he said, "There was a bilateral meeting with Iran. And India is in constant touch with Iran, and on areas in which there can be any cultural exchange, we are always in discussion. And discussions took place during the Summit too." The secretary said that during the bilateral meeting, "ideas have been thrown, though no such project has been concretised yet. But the discussions and engagements are on".

The three-day event was hosted by the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of External Affairs.

The Iranian Embassy in India in a post on X on Sunday said, at the civilisational summit, Tehran proposed setting up an "SCO Joint Network for Written Heritage and Civilisational Memory".

Dr Faridoddin Faridasr, Cultural Counsellor of the Islamic Republic of Iran in India, addressed the First SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi, highlighting the importance of shared civilisational heritage as a foundation for cultural cooperation and mutual understanding among SCO member states, it said.

In his remarks, he emphasised the historical role of the "Persian language as a language of science, literature, administration and cultural exchange across Central Asia, the Indian subcontinent and neighbouring regions, describing it as an important part of the shared cultural and historical heritage of the region".

Referring to Iran's successful cultural cooperation with India, he highlighted the activities of the Noor International Microfilm Centre, affiliated with the Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran in New Delhi. Since 1990, the Centre has collaborated with 72 academic and cultural institutions in India, resulting in the digitisation of "more than 150,000 Persian and Arabic manuscripts," the restoration and preservation of over three million pages of historical documents, and the preparation of nearly 300 catalogues, the embassy said.

Faridasr also referred to the ongoing joint projects with cultural institutions in Telangana and Hyderabad for the digitisation, restoration and preservation of historical Persian documents and manuscripts.

As a practical initiative to strengthen regional cultural cooperation, he proposed the establishment of an "SCO Joint Network for Written Heritage and Civilizational Memory." "The proposed network would focus on the preservation and digitisation of manuscripts and historical documents, the exchange of technical expertise and training in manuscript restoration, and the promotion of shared linguistic and literary heritage through joint research, publications and exhibitions," the embassy said in a detailed post on X.

He reaffirmed Iran's "readiness to share its experience and technical expertise with other SCO member states", stressing that the preservation of shared civilisational heritage provides an important opportunity to strengthen mutual trust, cultural understanding and cooperation across the region.

The forum was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on November 20. It saw the participation of delegates from various Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) member countries, including Pakistan, and other countries.

data.title: Like SpaceX, Anthropic ran an unusual IPO process, chafing some bankers
data.description:
For the second time this year, Wall Street bankers and lawyers took home a massive paycheck from a record-setting initial public offering. And for the second time this year, some of them came out of it complaining in private about how the process was riddled with complications and unlike any they had worked on before.
 
With SpaceX's IPO in June, in which banks earned half a billion dollars in fees, bankers chafed over how tightly the Elon Musk-led company controlled the months-long process and kept financial and other information private, making it hard for advisers to do their jobs.
 
As Anthropic's IPO, dubbed internally "Project Lantern", eclipsed SpaceX on Thursday and bankers took home more than half a billion dollars in fees, several people close to the process listed a litany of problems that had plagued the offering process: a compressed timeline, marred by last-minute changes and delays in sharing financial projections; rushed document approvals; and highly unusual restrictions on bankers and concern about leaks - especially after Reuters reported many details from a ‌draft IPO filing weeks before it was made public.
 
 
Anthropic, for example, instructed some of its 22 IPO underwriters to limit the number of ​bankers working on the deal to four, asking the firms to make sure they were senior staff, several people ​familiar with the matter said. One of the people said the restriction likely came out of fear that information would leak, and that the banks found a way to work around it anyway.
 
Underlying these complaints is a new power dynamic between technology companies and Wall Street. Companies ​such as SpaceX, Anthropic - and potentially also OpenAI in the future - have come to wield enormous power as the transformative potential of artificial intelligence creates a frenzied demand for their shares, and they are wielding it to do things their way. That is upsetting some bankers. But banks and investors appear to have little choice but to play along.
 
"These companies certainly did have some market power to tell underwriters that it's not going to be business as usual," said Jay Ritter, a University of Florida professor emeritus who researches IPOs. "But the big Wall Street firms, I suspect, are still going to be doing things as business as usual for all but maybe OpenAI (after these two deals)."
 
Ritter added that both SpaceX and Anthropic had negotiated to pay underwriters nothing on the additional shares sold through the greenshoe option. "I don't think most companies are going to be able to demand zero spread on ​overallotment shares," he said.
 
Anthropic, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, the two lead underwriters on the two IPOs, declined to comment.
 
SpaceX and OpenAI did not respond to requests for comment.
 
Both SpaceX and Anthropic debuted successfully, raising record amounts of money, and their shares rallied initially. A key part of the underwriters' job is to market the ‌securities. Thanks to the demand for AI, that was an easy sell - both companies had order books oversubscribed many times over.
 
After an initial burst in shares, the trajectories of the two big AI firms diverged. SpaceX climbed to a post-listing peak of $201.80 ​on June 16 before retreating below its $135 IPO price for the first time in mid-July. Anthropic's shares closed down 8.5% on Friday after a 17% first-day pop, as a dramatic unraveling of the AI trade showed that even a blockbuster listing could not shake the gloom hanging over the sector. 

UNUSUAL NON-COMPETES AND RESTRICTIONS

 
In the case of SpaceX's IPO, the people close to the process said Musk's team dictated terms at every stage. Musk's team told the largest and most powerful US banks - including Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley - how to market SpaceX's stock and to whom. It told some banks the specific order sizes they needed to "fill" - in some cases ‌a few billion dollars - and gave them instructions on what types of investors to bring. Banks signed on to underwrite ​the IPO without being told what they would be paid, the people said.
 
The underlying current running through Anthropic's IPO process was what ‌several of the people who spoke to Reuters interpreted as a sense of extreme caution.
 
Anthropic asked some senior officers at banks working on its IPO to sign legal documents restricting core members of the transaction team from working with rival companies, including OpenAI, Cursor, DeepSeek and ‌Hugging Face, for six months after it went public, according to the people.
 
Banks routinely manage conflicts and protect client confidentiality. But bankers and lawyers said it is rare for an IPO to impose exclusivity this broad, particularly on individual bankers.
 
In previous head-to-head IPOs such as those of ridesharing rivals Uber ​and Lyft, or real estate companies Trulia and Zillow, banks could simply pick a side, in part because the deals were smaller and required fewer banks.
 
Anthropic, by contrast, needed a broad syndicate to raise the enormous amount of capital it was seeking. That, some of the people said, explained why Anthropic sought to bind individual bankers with these restrictions.
 
One banker who declined to sign on to the agreement said it was a challenge to ​find people who could promise not to actively cover or engage with Anthropic's peers, especially as several of those companies pursue their own initial or secondary offerings. 

INFORMATION LEAKS AND LATE NIGHTS

 
Some of the restrictions were meant to control leaks of information.
 
Nearly four weeks before Anthropic's filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, called Form S-1, was made public, Reuters reported on it, revealing details of the company's financials, risk factors, dealings with other tech companies and other information.
 
Anthropic also used a product called NetRoadshow ‌to share information, instead of regular PDFs, with most of the banks underwriting the deal.
 
NetRoadshow logs access details, including information such as who has seen the document and looked at which page. Documents on NetRoadshow also had individual bankers' names as watermarks.
 
Leaks continued to surface in the press, but using NetRoadshow ‌complicated bankers' work, including because the platform would not let them save copies of documents, one of the people said.
 
Anthropic planned to file an updated securities filing, called an S-1A, with the SEC with the price range and to launch the marketing on November 10. To do so, it needed to send a draft to all the banks in its syndicate for them to sign off on it.
 
The night before it was to happen, a law firm on the deal sent a PDF to the banks about the sale of shares in Canada. But soon it followed with another email asking them to disregard it, saying it "contains incorrect price range and share information," according to the email, which was seen by Reuters.
 
The correct S-1A was then sent via the NetRoadshow platform around 2 a.m. New York time. Banks were told they had several hours to sign off on it before it was filed with the ​SEC.

data.title: China opposes ban on Chinese telecoms' direct access to US phone numbers
data.description:
China firmly opposes ​the US Federal Communications Commission's vote to ban Chinese telecommunications firms from direct access to US phone numbers, ‌its commerce ​ministry said ​on Sunday.
 
Thursday's FCC ​decision, which cited national security concerns, will bar China Mobile, China Telecom and China ​Unicom and other IP-enabled service ‌providers from direct access.
 
The ​regulator has pushed for decoupling the US and China in ‌the telecoms, ​communications, and ‌testing and certification sectors, the ‌Chinese ministry said in a ​statement, adding the actions run counter to the consensus ​reached by the countries' leaders.
 
China urged ‌the United States to retract ‌the ban, warning it would take necessary counter measures.

data.title: Iran attack hits civilian industrial facility in Bahrain, sparks fire
data.description:
Bahrain said on Saturday that an Iranian attack had hit a ​civilian industrial facility, causing a fire but no injuries, while Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they launched a missile-and-drone attack on US military positions in the kingdom, home to the US Navy's Fifth Fleet.
 
The incidents were the latest escalation of regional hostilities ‌since the US and Israel ​attacked Iran in February. Since ​then, Gulf Arab states have been drawn into the conflict, and there ​have been repeated Iranian attacks across the region.
 
Civil Defence teams were working to contain the fire at the industrial facility, the ministry said in a post on X. It gave no details on the ​location or nature of the site.
 
 
Bahrain's interior ministry initially issued ‌an alert urging residents to move to the nearest safe location because ​of a potential threat, without providing details. It later issued an all-clear before sending a second alert.
 
Later, Bahrain's Defence Force said its air defences had intercepted a ‌number of Iranian aerial ​attacks. Shrapnel from the interceptions caused ‌material damage but no casualties, it said, adding that Tehran was ‌continuing its "systematic hostile approach" towards the kingdom.
 
The Revolutionary Guards, in a statement ​carried by Iranian state news agency IRNA, said their aerospace forces had launched a combined missile-and-drone attack on US ​positions at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases "in retaliation for ongoing aggression and repeated violations of Iranian airspace."
 
US Central Command did ‌not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on the Guards' ‌account.
 
Bahrain has reported intercepting several Iranian aerial attacks in recent days. Gulf Arab states have come under repeated fire from Tehran since the war broke out.

data.title: Tata Steel to acquire 26.6% stake in APL Apollo for ₹15,510 crore
data.description:
Tata Steel on Monday announced a series of strategic transactions with APL Apollo Tubes, involving the sale of its steel tubes and colour-coated businesses, acquisition of a promoter stake in the company and a partnership to set up 5 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of colour-coated steel manufacturing capacity across India.
 
The company will acquire a 26.6 per cent promoter stake in APL Apollo for about ₹15,510 crore and launch an open offer for a further 26 per cent.
 
In a statement, the company said it had executed agreements for a comprehensive strategic partnership covering the sale of its steel tubes and colour-coated businesses to APL Apollo, the acquisition of the entire promoter stake of 26.6 per cent in APL Apollo, and a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with SG Tech Engineering Private Ltd (SG Spectra), a company associated with the promoter group of APL Apollo, to set up exclusive contract manufacturing facilities of 5 MTPA of colour-coated products on a modular and pan-India basis to leverage growth in the Indian colour-coated products market.
 

Deal structure

On Sunday, Tata Steel executed agreements to sell all its shareholding in Tata Steel Colors Pvt Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary, as well as its entire steel tubes business to APL Apollo Tubes Ltd.
 
This will consolidate Tata Steel’s surface-coated coil capacity of 800,000 tonnes per annum, as well as its 1.7 MTPA steel tubes business, in APL Apollo Pvt Ltd for a combined consideration of ₹28,000 crore.
 
APL Apollo will initially fund the acquisition through a mix of acquisition financing and subsequently replace the debt with long-term capitalisation to de-risk the balance sheet.
 
On Monday morning, Tata Steel executed agreements to acquire the 26.6 per cent promoter stake in APL Apollo Tubes Ltd at a price of ₹2,100 per share for a consideration of ₹15,510 crore.
 
Tata Steel will also make an open offer for an additional 26 per cent stake in APL Apollo Tubes Ltd at ₹2,301.40 per share for a consideration of ₹16,756 crore.
 
The transactions are subject to regulatory approvals, and Tata Steel expects to obtain these approvals in the coming months and close the composite set of transactions within FY27.

Downstream powerhouse

Tata Steel said that APL Apollo would now be the vehicle to drive downstream growth in steel tubes and colour-coated products. The new APL Apollo Tubes Pvt Ltd will build up to a 15.5 MTPA capacity by 2035, including 9 MTPA of steel tubes and 6.5 MTPA of colour-coated products.
 
The move is aimed at leveraging the combined strengths of the two companies, optimising capacity utilisation, unlocking value and improving profitability.
 
Commenting on the deal, T V Narendran, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Managing Director (MD) of Tata Steel, said: “We are very pleased to have entered into a comprehensive agreement with APL Apollo and the promoters as we create a downstream powerhouse for the future characterized by its inherent strengths of agility in the market, strong growth trajectory and benchmark capex-opex profile to serve the growing Indian market.”
 
This strategic move helps to consolidate the steel tubes and colour-coated businesses under Tata Steel’s ownership while unlocking multiple synergies between the two companies, he added. “This will create value for all stakeholders with enhanced customer centricity, pan-India reach, and a full product portfolio.”
 
Koushik Chatterjee, Executive Director (ED) and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Tata Steel, said: “We have over the last year emphasised our strategic intent to grow aggressively in the value-added space and expand our downstream footprint both organically and inorganically. While we have multiple projects under construction in value-added segments like tinplate and hot rolled pickled and galvanised lines, APL Apollo presented a unique opportunity for us.”
 
This is not just an acquisition of a very profitable and efficient company, but the best foundation to build a future business in the colour-coated space with an exclusive contract manufacturing agreement with SG Tech Engineering, an entity run by the promoters of APL Apollo, he said.
 
“Sanjay Gupta and his team have demonstrated experience in building downstream capacity with agility, speed and efficiency and this partnership will be very strategic for Tata Steel and APL Apollo in the future,” Chatterjee said, adding that APL Apollo not only adds growth from the first day with the transfer of Tata Steel’s business but also has the definite potential to be a very profitable 15.5 MTPA downstream company in the future.
